rules.title: Multiple if-else statements
rules.description: Using too many conditional if-else statements will impact performance since JVM will have to compare the conditions. Prefer using a switch statement instead of multiple if-else if possible, or refactor your code to reduce conditonnal statements on the same variable. Switch statement has a performance advantage over if - else.

rules.title: Getting the size of the collection in the loop
rules.description: When iterating over any collection, fetch the size of the collection in advance to avoid fetching it on each iteration, this saves CPU cycles, and therefore consumes less power.

rules.title: Use global variables
rules.description: When using a global variable, the interpretation engine must check: 1) that it exists in the current scope, in the one above, etc. ; 2) the variable has a value; 3) ... To avoid all these checks, it is often possible to pass the useful variables as arguments of routines, making them local. This process saves computational time (CPU cycles).

rules.title: Usage of preparedStatement instead of Statement
rules.description: SQL will only commit the query once, whereas if you used only one statement, it would commit the query every time and thus induce unnecessary calculations by the CPU and therefore superfluous energy consumption.

rules.title: Rewrite native getter/setters

rules.title: Initialize builder/buffer with the appropriate size
rules.description: If you know in advance how many characters would be appended, initialize builder/buffer with the appropriate size. They will thus never have to be resized. This saves CPU cycles and therefore consumes less energy.

rules.title: Using try...catch calls (on File Not Found error)
rules.description: When an exception is thrown, a variable (the exception itself) is created in the catch block and destroyed at the end of the block. Creating this variable and destroying it consumes CPU cycles and RAM unnecessarily. That is why it is important not to use this construction and to prefer, as much as possible, a logical test. This new rule replace old GCI34 only for a particular use case (FileNotFoundException)

rules.description: The shape using the quotation marks allows the developer to insert variables that will be substituted at run time. But if the string does not have a variable, use quotes instead. rules.title: Usage of static collections
rules.description: Avoid usage of static collections. If you want to use static collections make them final and create for example a singleton if needed containing the collections. The static fields are more complicated for the Garbage Collector to manage and can lead to memory leaks.

rules.title: Usage Pattern.compile() in a non-static context
rules.description: Avoid using Pattern.compile() in a non-static context. This operation requires a non negligible amount of computational power, Using a single match saves CPU cycles and RAM consumption.

rules.title: Const parameter in batch update
rules.description: Don't set const parameter in batch update => Put its in query. Creating this parameter and destroying it consumes CPU cycles and RAM unnecessarily.

rules.title: Free resources
rules.description: try-with-resources Statement needs to be implemented for any object that implements the AutoCloseable interface, it save computer resources.

rules.title: Specify struct layouts

rules.title: Make variable constant
rules.description: A variable is never reassigned and can be made constant

rules.title: Replace Enum ToString() with nameof

rules.title: Avoid async void methods
rules.description: Use async Task methods instead, for performance, stability and testability

rules.title: Make type sealed
rules.description: Seal types that don't need inheritance for performance reasons

rules.title: GC.Collect should not be called
rules.description: In most cases, the cost of calling GC.Collect far outweighs the benefits

rules.title: Use collection indexer

rules.title: Dispose resource asynchronously

rules.title: Use `Cast` instead of `Select` to cast

rules.title: Use string.Length instead of comparison with empty string
rules.description: Comparing a string to an empty string is unnecessary and can be replaced by a call to `string.Length` which is more performant and more readable.

rules.title: Return `Task` directly
rules.description: Consider returning a `Task` directly instead of a single `await`

rules.title: Use orElseGet instead of orElse
rules.description: Parameter of orElse() is evaluated, even when having a non-empty Optional. Supplier method of orElseGet passed as an argument is only executed when an Optional value isn’t present. Therefore, using orElseGet() will save computing time.

rules.title: Avoid querying SQL columns that are not used

rules.title: Optimize square computation (scalar vs vectorized method)

rules.title: Avoid raising Runtime Exceptions when a check is possible

rules.title: Data : Avoid CSV Format
rules.description: The Parquet format is faster to write to, lighter in weight and faster to read data from. It is suitable for use cases where there would be a lot of data I/O, especially with Cloud storage.

rules.title: Don't use .items() to iterate over a dictionary when only keys or values are needed
rules.description: Avoid using `.items()` if you only use the key or the value, as this creates an unnecessary tuple, leading to increased memory allocation and slower execution.

rules.title: Data / AI : PyTorch - Create tensors directly from Torch
rules.description: In PyTorch, prefer creating tensors directly using `torch.rand`, `torch.tensor`, or other Torch methods instead of converting from NumPy arrays. Avoid using `torch.tensor(np.random.rand(...))` or similar patterns when the same result can be achieved directly with PyTorch.

rules.title: Data : Avoid Iterative Matrix Operations

rules.title: Prefer Append Left

rules.title: Avoid Using Exceptions for Control Flow
rules.description: Using exceptions for control flow (loops, defaults, branching) is expensive in Python. Prefer idiomatic alternatives like dict.get(), enumerate(), getattr() with defaults, or proper iteration patterns.

rules.title: Python: Avoid wildcard imports (`from module import *`)
